demoDataNotice: DEMO DATA FOR ACADEMIC DEMONSTRATION ONLY. This is a small, hand-curated subset of well-documented drug-drug interactions, compiled for a final-year project to demonstrate a deterministic rule/dataset matching engine. It is NOT a complete or clinically validated interaction database and MUST NOT be used to make treatment decisions. Always consult a pharmacist or doctor. For production use, replace this file with a licensed dataset (for example DrugBank, RxNorm + NLM DDI, or a national formulary feed) using the same record shape.
sourceNotes: Interaction pairs and severity bands were compiled from widely published, non-proprietary drug interaction summaries (national formulary monographs and standard pharmacology references) and reduced to a teaching subset. No interaction in this file was generated by a language model.

severityScale.major: Clinically significant. The combination is usually avoided, or requires close medical supervision.
severityScale.moderate: May require dose adjustment, extra monitoring, or spacing the doses apart.
severityScale.minor: Usually manageable. Worth being aware of, rarely requires a change.

interactions.description: Both medicines reduce the blood's ability to clot. Taken together they substantially increase the risk of bleeding, including stomach bleeding.
interactions.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet effect; aspirin also irritates the stomach lining.
precautions: Do not start or stop either medicine without medical advice.
Watch for unusual bruising, nosebleeds, black stools or blood in urine.
Report any of these signs to your doctor immediately.

interactions.description: Anti-inflammatory painkillers increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin and can raise the INR.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID antiplatelet effect plus gastric irritation, added to warfarin anticoagulation.
precautions: Ask your doctor about a safer painkiller such as paracetamol.
If both are prescribed, INR monitoring is usually increased.

interactions.description: Metronidazole can raise warfarin levels sharply, increasing bleeding risk.
interactions.mechanism: Inhibition of the liver enzymes that clear warfarin (CYP2C9).
precautions: INR is usually checked more often during and after the antibiotic course.
Report unusual bleeding or bruising promptly.

interactions.description: This antibiotic can increase the effect of warfarin and the risk of bleeding.
interactions.mechanism: Reduced warfarin metabolism and altered gut flora that produce vitamin K.
precautions: Extra INR monitoring is usual during the antibiotic course.

interactions.description: Ibuprofen can block the heart-protective effect of low-dose aspirin, and the pair raises the risk of stomach irritation.
interactions.mechanism: Competition for the same platelet COX-1 binding site; additive gastric irritation.
precautions: If both are needed, take low-dose aspirin at least 30 minutes before ibuprofen.
Take with or after food and report stomach pain.

interactions.description: Fluid loss from a diuretic can reduce kidney function, which raises metformin levels.
interactions.mechanism: Reduced renal clearance of metformin during dehydration.
precautions: Keep well hydrated.
Kidney function is usually checked periodically.

interactions.description: This antibiotic sharply raises statin levels, increasing the risk of muscle damage.
interactions.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition reduces atorvastatin breakdown.
precautions: The statin is often paused for the duration of the antibiotic course.
Report muscle pain, tenderness or dark urine immediately.

interactions.description: The combination markedly increases simvastatin levels and the risk of muscle breakdown.
interactions.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition.
precautions: This combination is normally avoided; ask your doctor.

interactions.description: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the gut and reduces how much is absorbed.
interactions.mechanism: Formation of an insoluble complex in the gastrointestinal tract.
precautions: Separate the doses by at least 4 hours.
Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, usually first thing in the morning.

interactions.description: Reduced stomach acid can lower levothyroxine absorption slightly.
interactions.mechanism: Higher gastric pH reduces dissolution of levothyroxine tablets.
precautions: Take levothyroxine at a consistent time each day and mention this pair at your next thyroid test.

interactions.description: Calcium substantially reduces the absorption of this antibiotic, which can make it ineffective.
interactions.mechanism: Chelation of the fluoroquinolone by divalent cations.
precautions: Take the antibiotic 2 hours before, or 6 hours after, any calcium product or antacid.

interactions.description: Amlodipine raises simvastatin levels, increasing the risk of muscle side effects.
interactions.mechanism: Partial CYP3A4 inhibition.
precautions: The simvastatin dose is usually capped at 20 mg per day with amlodipine.
Report unexplained muscle pain.

interactions.description: SSRIs combined with aspirin increase the risk of stomach bleeding.
interactions.mechanism: SSRIs reduce platelet serotonin, adding to aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
precautions: Report stomach pain, black stools or vomiting blood.
Stomach protection may be prescribed.

interactions.description: Together these can cause serotonin syndrome, a rare but serious reaction.
interactions.mechanism: Additive serotonergic activity.
precautions: Seek urgent help for agitation, fever, shivering, fast heartbeat, muscle twitching or confusion.
Alternative pain relief is often preferred.

interactions.description: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome and of seizures.
interactions.mechanism: Additive serotonergic effect plus reduced tramadol metabolism.
precautions: Discuss alternative pain relief with your doctor.

interactions.description: Steroids and anti-inflammatory painkillers together markedly increase the risk of stomach ulcers.
interactions.mechanism: Additive damage to the gastric mucosa.
precautions: Take both with food.
Stomach protection is often prescribed.
Report stomach pain or black stools.

interactions.description: Steroids raise blood sugar and can work against diabetes treatment.
interactions.mechanism: Glucocorticoid-induced insulin resistance.
precautions: Monitor blood sugar more closely while taking the steroid.
Your diabetes dose may need temporary adjustment.

interactions.description: Penicillins can reduce methotrexate clearance, raising its toxicity.
interactions.mechanism: Competition for renal tubular secretion.
precautions: Blood counts are usually monitored.
Report mouth ulcers, sore throat or unusual tiredness.

interactions.description: Both can prolong the heart's QT interval, raising the risk of a dangerous rhythm disturbance.
interactions.mechanism: Additive QT prolongation.
precautions: An ECG is often required.
Report palpitations, dizziness or fainting.

interactions.description: Anti-inflammatory painkillers reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect and can strain the kidneys.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID inhibition of renal prostaglandins.
precautions: Use the lowest effective painkiller dose for the shortest time.
Keep hydrated; kidney function may be checked.

interactions.description: Reduced blood-pressure control and increased strain on the kidneys.
interactions.mechanism: NSAID inhibition of renal prostaglandins.
precautions: Prefer paracetamol for routine pain relief if suitable for you.

interactions.description: Beta blockers can reduce the effect of a reliever inhaler and may worsen asthma.
interactions.mechanism: Beta-adrenergic antagonism opposing beta-agonist bronchodilation.
precautions: Tell your doctor if your inhaler feels less effective.
Cardioselective beta blockers are usually preferred in asthma.

interactions.description: Omeprazole can reduce how well clopidogrel works.
interactions.mechanism: CYP2C19 inhibition reduces conversion of clopidogrel to its active form.
precautions: An alternative acid-reducing medicine such as pantoprazole is often preferred.

interactions.description: Dual antiplatelet therapy is often prescribed deliberately, but it does raise bleeding risk.
interactions.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effect.
precautions: This pair is often intentional after a stent or heart attack - do not stop either without advice.
Report unusual bleeding.

interactions.description: Potassium loss from the diuretic increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.
interactions.mechanism: Hypokalaemia increases myocardial sensitivity to digoxin.
precautions: Potassium and digoxin levels are usually monitored.
Report nausea, visual changes or a slow pulse.

interactions.description: This antibiotic raises theophylline levels and can cause toxicity.
interactions.mechanism: CYP1A2 inhibition.
precautions: Report nausea, tremor, palpitations or restlessness.
Levels are usually monitored.

interactions.description: Alcohol during and shortly after a metronidazole course can cause severe flushing, nausea and vomiting.
interactions.mechanism: Disulfiram-like reaction from acetaldehyde accumulation.
precautions: Avoid alcohol during the course and for 48 hours afterwards.

interactions.description: Phenobarbital can reduce montelukast levels slightly.
interactions.mechanism: Enzyme induction increases montelukast clearance.
precautions: Mention any worsening asthma control at your next review.

interactions.description: Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by antihistamines.
interactions.mechanism: Additive central nervous system depression.
precautions: Avoid driving if you feel drowsy.

interactions.description: Regular high-dose paracetamol over several days can raise the INR slightly.
interactions.mechanism: Interference with vitamin K-dependent clotting factor synthesis.
precautions: Occasional use is generally fine.
Mention regular daily use to your anticoagulation clinic.

duplicateTherapyGroups.description: Taking more than one anti-inflammatory painkiller at the same time adds side effects without adding much pain relief.
precautions: Use only one NSAID at a time unless your doctor has specifically advised otherwise.
Watch for stomach pain or black stools.

duplicateTherapyGroups.description: More than one statin at a time increases the risk of muscle damage without added benefit.
precautions: Check with your doctor - normally only one statin is prescribed.

duplicateTherapyGroups.description: Two proton pump inhibitors together give no extra benefit.
precautions: Ask your pharmacist whether both are really needed.

duplicateTherapyGroups.description: Combining SSRIs increases the risk of serotonin syndrome.
precautions: Do not combine without specialist advice.

duplicateTherapyGroups.description: Paracetamol appears in many combination cold and pain products. Taking more than one can exceed the safe daily limit and damage the liver.
precautions: Check the label of every painkiller and cold remedy.
Do not exceed 4 g (usually 8 x 500 mg tablets) in 24 hours for an adult.
